summary: On 8 June 2021 one customer's valid configuration change triggered a latent bug in Fastly's software and 85 percent of its network returned errors. Fastly detected it within a minute and most of the network was back in under an hour.

overview.background: Fastly runs a global edge network that caches and serves content for many large sites. A software release on 12 May 2021 contained a bug that stayed hidden until a specific customer configuration setting was used.
systems: Sites that rely on Fastly for delivery
overview.impact: Fastly says 85 percent of its network returned errors. About 95 percent of the network was operating normally within 49 minutes.
overview.severity: Global, short and very visible. Fastly gives no formal severity label.
overview.gaps: The post does not give the bug's exact code, the customer or the number of affected sites. Times in the original are given in Central European Summer Time, converted to UTC here.

archNote: Fastly describes an edge network and a configuration push. The picture below is a simplified conceptual view, not Fastly's internal architecture.

timeline.e: A software release containing the bug is deployed.
A customer's valid configuration change triggers the bug and the disruption begins.
Fastly detects the disruption within a minute.
The customer configuration is identified as the trigger, about 40 minutes in.
The majority of the network is back.
Deployment of a permanent fix begins.

rootCause.trigger: A valid customer configuration change used a path that Fastly's code had never exercised.
rootCause.underlying: A bug introduced in the 12 May software release lay dormant until that exact combination of settings was used.
contributing: Testing did not cover the setting combination
A single change reached a large part of a global network
Customers share the same underlying software
propagation: Nodes with the buggy software fail on it.
85 percent of the network returns errors.
Sites that depend on the network fail.

evidence.label: Detection speed
evidence.body: Wir erkannten die Störung innerhalb einer Minute
evidence.note: German original from Fastly's blog; it means that the disturbance was detected within one minute.

evidence.label: Simulated edge error spike
evidence.body:
edge-fra-12  5xx_rate=0.88  req/s=41200
edge-lhr-03  5xx_rate=0.91  req/s=38700
edge-sin-07  5xx_rate=0.12  req/s=22100
evidence.note: Illustrative only. Fastly does not publish node-level metrics in the post.

evidence.label: Simulated canary gate
evidence.body:
rollout:
  stages: [1pct, 5pct, 25pct, 100pct]
  hold_minutes: 10
  abort_if:
    error_rate_over: 0.02
    compared_to: control_group
evidence.note: A teaching example of a staged rollout rule; not Fastly's configuration.

diagnose.step: Look for the first change that matches the start of the errors.
diagnose.why: Matching the first error time with change events finds a trigger fast.
Differences in version or setting show the trigger.

diagnose.step: Identify the customer or setting involved.
diagnose.why: Fastly did this about 40 minutes in.

correct.step: Revert or disable the triggering configuration.
correct.why: This stopped the errors and services returned.
Fastly began this later the same day.

verify.step: Confirm error rates and cache hit rates return to baseline.
Test the setting combination on a canary.
verify.why: Confirms the bug is fixed rather than hidden.

prevent.step: Roll out software and configuration in stages with automatic abort.
prevent.why: A bug then affects few users.

prevent.step: Add tests for rare setting combinations.
prevent.why: Fastly's post says it will review why testing missed the bug.
Fastly names WebAssembly isolation as a direction.

fix.safety: Reverting a customer's configuration affects that customer, so tell them. Never disable safety gates to speed up a rollout during an incident.

troubleshoot.scenario: Error rates jump to 85 percent in one minute across regions. No deployment happened today.
clues: A customer config was pushed minutes before
Nodes are all on the same version
troubleshoot.question: What do you look for, and in what order?
hints: Does config count as a change?
troubleshoot.answer: Treat configuration pushes as changes, find the one just before the spike, identify the setting, revert it, then investigate the underlying bug.

options: A dormant software bug triggered by a valid customer change
rootcause.why: Fastly says a May release contained a bug that a valid configuration change triggered.

remediation.task: Write a canary policy for configuration changes.
remediation.answer: Apply to 1 percent of nodes, hold ten minutes, compare error rates to a control group, abort automatically on a rise, then widen in stages.

remediation.task: Explain why detection speed was not enough.
remediation.answer: Detection took a minute but the impact was global at once, so the blast radius, not detection time, set the damage.
Post a status notice early, update regularly, name the trigger when confirmed, and publish a summary afterwards.

design.prompt: Design a configuration pipeline for a global network that makes one bad change affect under 1 percent of traffic.
constraints: Changes should reach users within minutes
design.answer: Stage changes by region and share, gate each step on independent health metrics, keep the previous version ready, and limit shared fate between customers through isolation.

checks.q: When was the bug-carrying software released?
checks.why: Fastly says the release was on 12 May 2021.

checks.q: What share of the network returned errors?
How long to reach 95 percent normal?
checks.why: Fastly says 95 percent operated normally within 49 minutes.

checks.q: Which prevents one change from reaching all nodes at once?
options: Staged rollout with a health gate

preventive: Staged rollout for software and configuration
monitoring: Alert on error rate within a minute
practices: Publish a clear summary after the incident

verification: Facts were read from Fastly's blog (German edition) on 29 October 2026. UTC times are our conversion. The architecture is Conceptual because Fastly did not publish internals; edge metrics and rollout configuration are Simulated.
